questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.topic: Subquery in a filter versus a join
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish a subquery filter from a join
questions.stem: A biologist's survey uses WHERE species_id IN (subquery) instead of a join; what does the subquery filter do?

options.text: It keeps only rows whose species is in the subquery result
It multiplies survey rows per species
It adds species columns to the result

questions.explanation: A subquery in a filter tests membership and keeps matching rows without multiplying or adding columns. A join would add columns and possibly multiply rows.

stimulus.body: SELECT * FROM observations o WHERE depth > (SELECT AVG(depth) FROM observations WHERE site_id=o.site_id).

questions.stem: In this survey query, how often does the correlated subquery execute?
questions.explanation: A correlated subquery references the outer row, so it runs once per outer row. An uncorrelated subquery runs once.

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.topic: Window function against group-by
questions.stem: A biologist's survey asks for per-site average depth alongside each observation; explain why a window function beats GROUP BY.

questions.explanation: GROUP BY collapses rows per site, losing individual observations. A window keeps all rows and adds the aggregate.
